subject.title: Anthropic setup-token onboarding path has multiple failure modes (docs gap, credential propagation, multi-agent sync)

question: Should Anthropic setup-token/manual token auth physically copy portable token profiles to sibling agent stores, rely on main-store read-through, or expose an explicit operator-controlled sync/doctor path?
rationale: The remaining fix affects credential isolation and upgrade semantics; source inspection proves current one-store writes and read-through coexist, while prior sibling-sync PRs showed that the wrong sync policy can copy sensitive OAuth material.

options.title: Prefer inheritance plus explicit repair
options.body: Keep read-through as the default, improve setup-token guidance and validation, and add an audited operator-controlled static-token sync or doctor repair path for cases that still need physical copies.

options.title: Auto-copy static tokens only
options.body: Automatically fan out Anthropic static token profiles during setup while preserving the existing OAuth non-portable policy and adding focused tests for every setup-token entry point.

options.title: Declare read-through sufficient
options.body: Close the propagation portion as covered by current runtime inheritance and track only prompt/docs or validation polish separately.

recommendation.title: Prefer inheritance plus explicit repair
recommendation.body: Keep read-through as the default, improve setup-token guidance and validation, and add an audited operator-controlled static-token sync or doctor repair path for cases that still need physical copies.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent commits on the affected auth-write paths and already surfaced the auth-file security concern on a related PR.
